fact: DataXion operates a data centre in Tunisia offering availability of 99.995% to its customers; page dated 2024-05-31 by its metadata.
DataXion states it is the only Tunisian data centre certified Tier IV by the Uptime Institute (operator claim, undated beyond the page date 2024-05-31).
EO Datacenter (Meninx Holding), a hosting operator described as leader of hosting in Tunisia, was operating and obtained PCI-DSS certification; also ISO 27001.
Orange Tunisie and EO Data Center (Meninx Holding) signed an MoU on housing/hosting offers (U, quarter or half rack, dedicated racks) across EO's Tunis and Enfidha sites.
The article says EO Data Center is designed to Tier III+ across its Tunis and Enfidha sites (design claim, no certification named).
Meninx Technologies, the first neutral data centre in Tunisia, based in Enfidha, was operating and was renamed EO Data Center; it offers hosting and cloud backup to customers.

Meninx Technologies officially inaugurated Meninx Data Centre at Enfidha, 100 km from Tunis, on 10 May 2013, described as Tunisia's first private neutral data centre hosting clients' IT and telecom equipment, with a first 250 m2 of equipped rooms extensible to 1,000 m2.
Tunisie Telecom states its Carthage data centre, in service since 2014, is dedicated to colocation, cloud computing and cybersecurity services for businesses.

Orange Tunisie inaugurated a new 1,000 m2 data centre at Kalaa Kebira, Sousse, serving its own needs and B2B customers with hosting, cloud and backup; the document gives no event date, so its published date 2025-05-06 is used.

Orange Tunisie states its new Kalaa Kebira, Sousse data centre has a technical environment conforming to the Tier III standard (operator statement, no certifier named); the document gives no event date, so its published date 2025-05-06 is used.

OnTech.tn reports Orange Tunisie unveiled its new 1,000 m2 data centre at Kalaa Kebira, Sousse, offering colocation, dedicated hosting and private or hybrid cloud to clients; the document gives no event date, so its published date 2025-05-05 is used.

OnTech.tn reports the Orange Tunisie Kalaa Kebira, Sousse data centre was designed and built to the Tier III standard with N+1 redundancy, and quotes Orange executives citing Tier III certification, without naming a certifier; the document gives no event date, so its published date 2025-05-05 is used.

A Tunisie Telecom presentation to ITU/ALECSO describes its Carthage primary data centre (2,700 m2, 200 racks) offering corporate housing (space, power, cooling, security) and an IaaS cloud platform set up in 2015; no event date is given beyond the deck's date 2018-10-29.

Tunisie Telecom's Carthage Data Center has been operational since June 2014, offering hosting and outsourcing of information systems to large, medium and small enterprises; its ISO/IEC 27001:2013 certification was maintained by TUV Rheinland in May 2017 (no Tier rating stated).

Tunisie Telecom installed its new Kasbah (Tunis) Data Centre, a 280 m2 server room with 92 racks, to offer corporate clients (ministries, administrations, banks) colocation, dedicated or shared hosting, managed services and SaaS; date taken from the article's published date, 2010-09-06.

Ooredoo's Capital Markets Day deck says its carrier-neutral data centre platform Syntys is active in Tunisia, with about 2 MW of current capacity and a 25% share of the Tunisian data centre market, offering colocation, cloud and AI hosting; no tier rating is given.
DataXion, a multi-operator colocation datacentre in Tunis owned by Poulina Group Holding, was inaugurated in May 2016 and offers IT housing to businesses (1,200 m2 over four rooms of 400 kW each).

DataXion states it is the only Tier IV-certified datacentre in Tunisia (operator's own claim; the certifying body is not named on the page); as_of is the page's published date as it gives no certification date.

Tunisie Telecom's Data Center Carthage has been operational since June 2014 and offers hosting and outsourcing of IT systems and cloud services to large, medium and small enterprises (WebManagerCenter, 2017-07-11).
Data centres dataset: Tunisie Telecom Carthage Data Center (Tunisie Telecom), colocation/carrier-neutral, in service; this document names it (published 2014-08-01).
Ooredoo Tunisie's own page offers its 188 m2 TIA-942-conformant data centre to business customers as rented racks, cages and shared racks (Housing), with a 99.95% SLA and a 24-month minimum term.
DataXion's own page says its cloud for AI rests on a 'Tier IV' datacentre in Tunisia with 99.995% availability, selling GPU cloud capacity to companies.
EO Data Center received the G-Cloud label in July 2024 as a Tunisian hosting provider supplying cloud services to public structures.
The ANCS register of 20 November 2025 lists Tunisie Telecom, Dataxion and Ooredoo Tunisie as N-Cloud labelled providers offering colocation space.
